newsitem.title: USA: BOXING-TYSON TESTIFIES IN TRAINER'S LAWSUIT.
newsitem.headline: BOXING-TYSON TESTIFIES IN TRAINER'S LAWSUIT.

text.p: Heavyweight boxing champion Mike Tyson said in court on Monday he had considered rehiring former trainer Kevin Rooney before Rooney sued him for $49 million.

Tyson testified in a lawsuit filed by Rooney, who claims he is owed $750,000 for training Tyson to fight Frank Bruno in the late 1980s. Rooney also says he had been verbally promised a lifetime contract to train the boxer by Tyson's former manager and mentor Cus D'Amato.
"I considered bringing him back until he sued me," Tyson said during three hours of testimony before a federal jury in Albany, New York. "I don't hate Kevin."

Tyson fired Rooney in 1988 after Rooney publicly commented about the boxer's failed marriage to Robin Givens. Rooney had worked with Tyson since the athlete's amateur days in 1982 until Tyson became world champion in 1988.
"Even right now I am not mad at him," said Tyson, looking straight at Rooney in a courtroom crowded with spectators. "We were like brothers and very tight friends."

However, later in his testimony, Tyson did show anger toward Rooney and visibly choked back tears when discussing D'Amato, who helped Tyson make the journey from reform school to boxing glory. D'Amato died in 1985.

After Tyson finished his testimony Monday, his lawyers filed a motion to have the case dismissed, but Chief Judge Thomas McAvoy reserved judgment, and the jurors were expected to hear more witnesses Tuesday.

On the stand last week, Rooney said D'amato, Tyson's guardian, had promised him a lifetime job with a guaranteed 10 percent cut of the boxer's winnings. He said there was a tradition in the boxing industry of honouring verbal contracts and he felt betrayed.
The boxer has said there was no such deal or at least none he knew about.
Rooney said in his lawsuit that he was entitled to 10 percent of Tyson's net worth, which Rooney calculated at $490 million.
Tyson, who apparently had written contracts with other trainers, told the court he never used "paper contracts" with Rooney.
The trial of Rooney's lawsuit was postponed by Tyson's conviction in 1992 and prison sentence for the rape of a 19-year-old black beauty contestant from Rhode Island. Tyson was paroled in March 1995.
Two weeks ago, Tyson stopped Bruce Seldon in one minute and 49 seconds of the first round to win the World Boxing Association (WBA) heavyweight title, his fourth victory since his parole.

His next opponent is scheduled to be former champion Evander Holyfield in November. Last March, Tyson won the World Boxing Council (WBC) title by beating Frank Bruno of Britian in his third comeback fight.
The trial, which began last Tuesday with jury selection, is being held in Albany because Rooney lives nearby.
